title: The Tamil Fleet That Sailed to Srivijaya

lines.text: In the year ten twenty five, a Tamil fleet sailed out into the open sea.
lines.caps: in the year *1025 | a *Tamil fleet sailed out | into the open *sea.

lines.text: Its target was Srivijaya, a sea power on the far side of the Bay of Bengal.
lines.caps: its target was *Srivijaya | a sea power | across the *Bay of Bengal.

lines.text: The Chola emperor Rajendra had sent it.
lines.caps: the Chola emperor *Rajendra | had sent it.

lines.text: Chola ships first struck Palembang, the capital, its palace and its monasteries.
lines.caps: first they struck *Palembang | the capital | its palace | its *monasteries.

lines.text: An inscription at Thanjavur says the Srivijayan king was taken prisoner.
lines.caps: an inscription at *Thanjavur | says the king | was taken *prisoner.

lines.text: It calls his land Kadaram, probably Kedah, on the Malay coast.
lines.caps: it calls his land *Kadaram | probably *Kedah | on the Malay coast.

lines.text: Why did the Cholas go? Historians disagree.
lines.caps: why did the Cholas go? | historians *disagree.

lines.text: Some say prestige, the glory of a world conqueror. Others say protecting trade with China.
lines.caps: some say *prestige | others say | protecting *trade with China.

lines.text: A Chinese writer says Srivijaya forced passing ships to stop at its ports.
lines.caps: a Chinese writer says | Srivijaya *forced ships | to stop at its ports.

lines.text: But he wrote about two centuries later.
lines.caps: but he wrote | about *two centuries later.

lines.text: Most historians see fast raids and plunder, not lasting rule.
lines.caps: most see *raids and plunder | not *lasting rule.

lines.text: Still, Srivijaya's grip on the sea trade was weakened.
lines.caps: still | Srivijaya's *grip on sea trade | was *weakened.

lines.text: Our main evidence is one Chola inscription.
lines.caps: our main evidence | is *one Chola inscription.

lines.text: A thousand years ago, a Tamil fleet reached across the sea, and shook a sea power.
lines.caps: a *thousand years ago | a Tamil fleet *reached across the sea | and shook a *sea power.

lines.text: Follow Aazhi for the next chronicle.

sources.title: Chola invasion of Srivijaya (Wikipedia)
sources.supports: 1025-1026 naval invasions under Rajendra I; Palembang sacked incl. palace and monasteries; king captured per Thanjavur inscription; motives debated (prestige or trade with China); mostly raids and plunder, no lasting control; Srivijaya weakened; evidence mostly Chola inscriptions

sources.title: Lord of the ocean (The Week, 2020)
sources.supports: expedition 1025 CE; Palembang ransacked; only one inscription (Thanjavur) marks it; names Kadaram linked to Kedah; Zhao Rukuo, 13th century, says Srivijaya forced ships to call at its ports; motives debated; Malay marriage account is from a different tradition

illustration: All imagery is an artist's illustration; ship and fleet designs are generic and not drawn from a surviving Chola ship (none survives); no portrait of any king; no inscription text reproduced.
uncertain: motives; whether Kadaram is Kedah; whether the campaign was raid or conquest; claims about fleet size, ports counted, elephants or weapons are omitted because single or weak sources; Malay Annals marriage story omitted; Chinese writer is about two centuries after the event.
story_device: Night navigation by monsoon stars: a map of the Bay of Bengal crossing, ship's wake and star compass, port-by-port ledger of harbours dropping to a single inscription slab; ending on a harbour at dawn (must differ from ep1 and ep2)
